LOOK_AT.say: A surveyor's stake, gray with age, driven in by the right-hand opening.
repeat: Somebody surveyed this, once. I can't think what. There's nothing in here a man would want a boundary round.
I gave it a push. It didn't move. Whoever put it here meant it.

LISTEN_TO.say: A drip landing on its top, every few seconds.
repeat: The drip has worn a little cup in the wood.
Quiet. It's held its position longer than I've been alive.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's driven in to the knee. Taking it would mean digging, and I came here to walk.
overrides.TALK_TO: I said good morning to it. It's been standing here so long, I felt it was owed.

exits.name: THE WAY OUT

LOOK_AT.say: Daylight, and the washout, and a mule who's glad I've gone.
repeat: The way I came in. I know where it goes. That's a comfort, down here.
I can see Grievance's tail flicking, out in the bright. She hasn't followed me. She isn't going to.
Wind across the mouth of the mine.
A crow, outside, still laughing.

overrides.TALK_TO: I called out to Grievance that I was all right. She didn't ask.

exits.note: Doc 108: daylight, the way he came in.

exits.name: THE LEFT OPENING

LOOK_AT.say: An opening in the rock, timbered, going down into the dark.
repeat: The timbers are good. That tells me someone came back out.
I've stood in front of it long enough that it's starting to look like a decision.
Air, moving a little.
Air, and a drip. The same as the others, near enough.
